title: Identification of potential regulating effect of baicalin on NFkappaB/CCL2/CCR2 signaling pathway in rats with cerebral ischemia by antibody-based array and bioinformatics analysis.
authors: Xu, Tian; Wang, Xueqian; Ma, Chongyang; Ji, Jing; Xu, Wenxiu; Shao, Qi; Liao, Xuejing; Li, Ying; Cheng, Fafeng; Wang, Qingguo
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄苓苷对脑缺血大鼠NFkappaB/CCL2/CCR2通路的调控，含分子对接和转录因子预测，但核心是炎症信号通路而非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Baicalin is one of the major bioactive compounds extracted from the root of Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi, which was used to treat cerebral ischemia for thounds of years. However, its biological mechanisms remains to be further explored. AIM OF THE REVIEW: This study aims to identify potential biological mechanisms of baicalin against cerebral ischemia combining antibody-based array and bioinformatics analysis. METHODS: A rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was constructed. Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly divided into three groups: control group, ischemic model group, and baicalin 100 mg/kg treatment group respectively. Bederson score and 2, 3, 5-triphenyl tetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining were examined to evaluate the pharmacodynamics of baicalin treatment. Antibody-based array technology, enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), western-blot, molecular docking, transcription factor perdiction, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), and immunofluorescence staining were used to study the regulation of baicalin on inflammatory response after cerebral ischemia in vivo. LPS-induced RAW 264.7 macrophage inflammation model was prepared to observe the anti-inflammatory effect of baicalin in vitro. RESULTS: Baicalin (100 mg/kg) reduced neurological injury score, cerebral infarction volume, and necrotic cells in MCAO rats. Baicalin inhibited the expression of CCL2, and reduced the phosphorylation levels of p65, IkappaBalpha protein and down-regulated level of CCR2. Besides, baicalin could bond to CCR2 directly, which prevented CCL2 from binding to CCR2. Furthermore, baicalin down-regulated the number of monocytes in the peripheral blood and improved the spleen index post-cerebral ischemia. In vitro, baicalin significantly inhibited the secretion of NO, IL6, TNFalpha, and CCL2 in macrophages and promoted the secretion of IL13, IFNG, and IL1a. CONCLUSIONS: Baicalin inhibited cerebral ischemia-induced activation of the NFkappaB/CCL2/CCR2 pathway with multiple target effect. These data promote the therapeutic utilization of baicalin in preventing cerebral ischemia clinically.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：黄芩苷是从黄芩（Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi）根部提取的主要生物活性化合物之一，数千年来被用于治疗脑缺血。然而，其生物学机制仍有待进一步探索。综述目的：本研究旨在结合基于抗体的阵列和生物信息学分析，识别黄芩苷抗脑缺血的潜在生物学机制。方法：构建大鼠大脑中动脉闭塞（MCAO）模型。将Sprague-Dawley大鼠随机分为三组：对照组、缺血模型组和黄芩苷100 mg/kg治疗组。通过Bederson评分和2,3,5-三苯基四氮唑氯化物（TTC）染色评估黄芩苷治疗的药效学。采用基于抗体的阵列技术、酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）、蛋白质印迹、分子对接、转录因子预测、苏木精-伊红（H&E）和免疫荧光染色，研究黄芩苷在体内对脑缺血后炎症反应的调控。制备LPS诱导的RAW 264.7巨噬细胞炎症模型，以观察黄芩苷在体外的抗炎作用。结果：黄芩苷（100 mg/kg）降低了MCAO大鼠的神经损伤评分、脑梗死体积和坏死细胞数量。黄芩苷抑制CCL2的表达，降低p65、IkappaBalpha蛋白的磷酸化水平，并下调CCR2水平。此外，黄芩苷可直接与CCR2结合，从而阻止CCL2与CCR2的结合。进一步地，黄芩苷下调外周血中单核细胞数量，并改善脑缺血后的脾指数。在体外，黄芩苷显著抑制巨噬细胞中NO、IL6、TNFalpha和CCL2的分泌，并促进IL13、IFNG和IL1a的分泌。结论：黄芩苷通过多靶点效应抑制脑缺血诱导的NFkappaB/CCL2/CCR2通路激活。这些数据促进了黄芩苷在临床预防脑缺血中的治疗应用。
